The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal) |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX A6000 (Google Cloud calls it `nvidia-tesla-a6000`) |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM) – you can adjust this to your needs |
| **Zone** | `us-central1-a` (pick a zone that supports GPUs) |
| **Project** | `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` (replace with your actual project ID) |
| **Instance name** | `rtx-a6000-ubuntu` |

---

## 1. Prerequisites

1. **Enable the Compute Engine API**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com
   ```

2. **Enable the GPU API**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com
   ```

3. **Create a service account with the `roles/compute.admin` role** (or use your own credentials).  
   ```bash
   gcloud iam service-accounts create gpu-sa \
     --display-name="GPU Service Account"
   gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
     --member="serviceAccount:gpu-sa@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
     --role="roles/compute.admin"
   ```

4. **Set the default project and zone**  
   ```bash
   gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID
   gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a
   ```

5. **Make sure you have enough quota for GPUs** – request a quota increase if needed.

---

## 2. Create the instance with `gcloud`

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --machine-type n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size 100GB \
  --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags http-server,https-server
```

### Explanation of the flags

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--boot-disk-type` | SSD for better I/O |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--maintenance-policy TERMINATE` | If the host is reclaimed, the VM is terminated (recommended for GPU workloads) |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart on crash |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Optional: run a startup script (e.g., install CUDA drivers) |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic (if you need a web server) |

> **Tip:** If you want to use the **REST API** instead of `gcloud`, see the JSON payload below.

---

## 3. REST API (curl) Example

```bash
# Replace YOUR_PROJECT_ID, YOUR_ZONE, and YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# JSON payload
read -r -d '' PAYLOAD <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the API call
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances?alt=json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$PAYLOAD"
```

> **Note:**  
> * The `acceleratorType` URL uses the project ID because GPU types are project‑scoped.  
> * The `startup-script` installs CUDA drivers automatically. Adjust as needed.

---

## 4. Verify the instance

```bash
gcloud compute instances list --filter="name=$INSTANCE_NAME"
```

You should see the instance status as `RUNNING`. SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh $INSTANCE_NAME
```

Once inside, verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

## 5. Clean up

When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid incurring charges:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete $INSTANCE_NAME --quiet
```

---

### Quick Reference

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `gcloud compute instances create ...` | CLI method |
| `curl ...` | REST API method |
| `gcloud compute instances list` | List instances |
| `gcloud compute ssh` | SSH into instance |
| `nvidia-smi` | Check GPU status |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or add more GPUs if your workload requires it. Happy GPU computing!
